rationale: The complete canonical README is retained byte for byte. The specification quantifies every entrywise nonnegative real p-by-q matrix with ordinary real rank exactly three and real PSD rank exactly two, and then every fixed size-two PSD factorization. Rank three excludes empty dimensions without needing an extra dimension restriction.

A size-k factorization is concretely the family of real symmetric PSD matrices satisfying every exact trace product equation. Existence at k=2 together with nonexistence at k=1 is exactly minimum PSD size two because the canonical minimum ranges over integers k>=1; no k=0 loophole occurs.

Feasible directions retain real symmetric E_i,F_j, every first-order equation trace(E_i*B_j)+trace(A_i*F_j)=0 and one common h>0 such that every perturbed factor is PSD for every 0<=t<h. This is the actual straight-line condition. It neither weakens it to an unsupported tangent-cone assertion nor strengthens it to exact factorization at positive t.

The rigidity clause uses one shared real scalar d with E_i=d*A_i and F_j=-d*B_j for all factors. The uniqueness clause quantifies every other real size-two factorization and one invertible real S shared by the entire family, with Atilde_i=S^T*A_i*S and Btilde_j=S^-1*B_j*(S^-1)^T. This preserves both congruence direction and inverse/transpose order.

The proposed equivalence retains both directions and every fixed original factorization. Zeros, singular and repeated factors, and zero rows or columns are not excluded. There is no positive-entry, positive-definite or normalization assumption, and no replacement of exact equalities by tolerance tests.

The requirements that PSD, rank, trace, products and inverses expand to actual mathematical definitions are sufficient for a statement-only implementation. Invertibility must guard the inverse in the uniqueness clause. No analytic, numerical or computational proof of the equivalence is claimed by this specification review.
